extracted.intended_audience: broadcasters, petitioners, and interested commenters participating in FCC television allotment rulemaking proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria relevant to petitions for television channel allotments and the related FCC notice-and-comment rulemaking (demonstrating community status, engineering showings, filing comments, and procedural requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments filing deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be filed on or before February 20, 2024 and reply comments on or before March 4, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the stated deadlines for initial and reply comments; comments are no longer being accepted after the listed close date. Use the PDF linked in the document sidebar for the official electronic format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper filing procedures for comments
rubrics_metrics.description: See Sections 1.415 and 1.420 of the Commission's rules for information regarding the proper filing procedures for comments, 47 CFR 1.415 and 1.420.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the procedures in these cited rule sections when submitting comments to ensure they are properly filed and considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of documents / address for service
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to filing comments with the FCC, interested parties should serve counsel for the Petitioner as follows: Ari Meltzer, Wiley Rein LLP, 2050 M Street NW, Washington, DC 20036. Federal Communications Commission, Office of the Secretary, 45 L Street NE, Washington, DC 20554.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure service on the petitioner's counsel in addition to filing with the FCC as indicated to satisfy service expectations in the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte contacts prohibition (and exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the public should note that all ex parte contacts are prohibited from the time a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking is issued to the time the matter is no longer subject to Commission consideration or court review, see 47 CFR 1.1208.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware there are exceptions to this prohibition, which can be found in Section 1.1204(a) of the Commission's rules; consult those rules before engaging with Commission decisionmakers during the restricted period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community qualification for allotment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Petitioner states that Waynesboro qualifies as a community for allotment purposes, supporting that claim with facts: Waynesboro is an independent and principal city of the Staunton-Waynesboro Metropolitan Statistical Area; as of the 2020 Census Waynesboro had a population of 22,196 and the Staunton-Waynesboro Statistical Area had a population of 125,654; Waynesboro has its own ZIP Code, two post offices, city council, public school system, police department, and library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use similar demonstrable municipal and demographic attributes (population data, ZIP Code, local government, public services, schools, post offices, library, etc.) to show that an entity qualifies as a community for allotment purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: First local service / allotment priority (television allotment priority standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Petitioner's proposal would result in a first local service to Waynesboro under the second priority of the Commission's television allotment priority standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrating that an allotment would provide a first local service can satisfy Commission allotment priority criteria; compare proposals against the Commission's priority standard to determine relative merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum geographic spacing requirements (47 CFR 73.623(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Channel *12 can be allotted to Waynesboro, consistent with the minimum geographic spacing requirements for new allotments in section 73.623(d) of the Commission's rules (Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide engineering analyses showing compliance with the specific minimum spacing distances in 47 CFR 73.623(d); the Bureau's staff engineering analysis confirmed compliance for the specified allotment point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community coverage contour requirement (47 CFR 73.625(a)(1) and 43 dBμ contour)
rubrics_metrics.description: The allotment point complies with section 73.625(a)(1) of the Rules as the entire community of Waynesboro is encompassed by the proposed 43 dBμ contour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate via technical showing that the proposed allotment's predicted 43 dBμ (dB microvolt per meter) contour fully encompasses the community; provide coordinates and contour analyses to support the showing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engineering allotment point and technical showing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bureau staff engineering analysis confirms an allotment point at 37°38′24″ N and 78°27′11″ W (allotment point) meets applicable spacing and contour rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify precise allotment coordinates and include engineering exhibits/calculations to verify compliance with spacing, interference, and contour coverage rules when proposing an allotment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain-language summary requirement (Providing Accountability Through Transparency Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Providing Accountability Through Transparency Act requires each agency, in providing notice of a rulemaking, to post online a brief plain-language summary of the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include or consult the agency-posted plain-language summary (available at the FCC's proposed-rulemakings page) to understand and communicate the rulemaking in accessible terms as required by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility of materials
rubrics_metrics.description: To request materials in accessible formats (braille, large print, computer diskettes, or audio recordings), send an email to FCC504@fcc.gov or call the Consumer & Government Affairs Bureau at (202) 418-0530 (VOICE), (202) 418-0432 (TTY).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide or request accessible formats per the contact information so that individuals needing alternate formats can obtain rulemaking materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act and Regulatory Flexibility Act applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: This document does not contain information collection requirements subject to the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995. Provisions of the Regulatory Flexibility Act of 1980 do not apply to this proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm whether PRA or RFA analyses apply to a proposed rule; if no information collection or small-business impacts are implicated, state that these Acts do not apply as in this document.
